expect_red: every suite prints the registry key it was dispatched under — a --only filter is copied straight off that line, and every `suite` in scripts/mutation_witnesses/ is a whole copy of one

mutations.contract: A browser suite prints the label the SUITES registry dispatches it under. The key is the label, so a `--only` filter can be copied straight off a failing line and mutation_witnesses.json's `suite` values mean what they say.
mutations.note: mutation_witness_tier_repair single-sourced the labels and left the pass-through unobserved: dropping the argument left every tier green and printed `[undefined] 2/2 sub-checks passed: PASS`. --only filters on the registry key rather than the printed line, so even the mutation tier keeps working -- the damage is silent by construction. The originating issue's runtime check was dismissed as comparing a string to itself; it is not, once the in-body copies are gone. The key comes from the registry and result.label from whatever the suite body returned.
